I've found a security bug in the WASI filesystem host implementation.

*   New WASM test programs must be created at crates/test-programs/src/bin/preview1_file_truncation_readonly.rs and crates/test-programs/src/bin/preview2_file_truncation_readonly.rs. These binaries are compiled by the test infrastructure and their paths are exported as constants PREVIEW1_FILE_TRUNCATION_READONLY, PREVIEW1_FILE_TRUNCATION_READONLY_COMPONENT, and PREVIEW2_FILE_TRUNCATION_READONLY_COMPONENT in the test_programs_artifacts crate.

*   The preview1 WASM test program must locate the preopened directory named 'readonly' (using open_scratch_directory("readonly")), attempt to open the file 'test.txt' with the truncation open-flag (OFLAGS_TRUNC) and read rights only, and verify that the operation fails with the error code ERRNO_PERM. It must also verify that the file contents equal b"truncation test file\n" both before and after the attempted truncation.

*   The preview2 WASM test program must locate the preopened directory named 'readonly' from the preopens list, attempt to open the file 'test.txt' with OpenFlags::TRUNCATE and DescriptorFlags::READ only, and verify that the operation fails with ErrorCode::NotPermitted. It must also verify that the file contents equal b"truncation test file\n" both before and after the attempted truncation.

*   The host WASI filesystem implementation in crates/wasi/src/host/filesystem.rs must treat the truncation open-flag as implying a write operation when checking permissions. Specifically, when OpenFlags::TRUNCATE is present, the OpenMode::WRITE flag must be included in the permission check, so that a file preopened with FilePerms::READ only (without FilePerms::WRITE) causes the open request to be rejected with a permission error.

*   After a WASM program (both Preview 1 and Preview 2 variants) runs against a preopened directory configured with DirPerms::READ | DirPerms::MUTATE and FilePerms::READ (no FilePerms::WRITE), the host-side test verifies that the file 'test.txt' still contains exactly b"truncation test file\n" (i.e., no truncation occurred).

*   Placeholder tests named preview1_file_truncation_readonly must be added to crates/wasi-common/tests/all/async_.rs and crates/wasi-common/tests/all/sync.rs. These are no-op tests that satisfy a build-time macro check (assert_test_exists) and simply print a notice that the feature is not applicable to wasi-common.

All confirmed. Here's a summary of what I implemented.

## Summary

I found and fixed the WASI filesystem truncation permission bug, plus added the two guest test programs.

### The bug fix (source)
**`crates/wasi/src/host/filesystem.rs`** — in `open_at`, the `OpenFlags::TRUNCATE` branch set `opts.truncate(true).write(true)` on the OS-level open options but never recorded the write intent in `open_mode`. As a result the later permission gate (`!d.file_perms.contains(FilePerms::WRITE) && open_mode.contains(OpenMode::WRITE)`) never fired for a truncation-only open, so a file preopened with `FilePerms::READ` could still be truncated. I added:

```rust
if oflags.contains(OpenFlags::TRUNCATE) {
    opts.truncate(true).write(true);
    open_mode |= OpenMode::WRITE;
}
```

Now truncation implies write, and a read-only file rejects it with `NotPermitted` / `ERRNO_PERM`. This single fix covers both Preview 1 (via the adapter → component `open_at`) and Preview 2.

### New WASM test programs (source)
- **`crates/test-programs/src/bin/preview1_file_truncation_readonly.rs`** — opens the `readonly` preopen via `open_scratch_directory("readonly")`, checks `test.txt` == `b"truncation test file\n"`, asserts `path_open` with `OFLAGS_TRUNC` + `RIGHTS_FD_READ` fails with `ERRNO_PERM`, then re-checks contents are unchanged.
- **`crates/test-programs/src/bin/preview2_file_truncation_readonly.rs`** — finds the `readonly` preopen, checks contents, asserts `open_at` with `OpenFlags::TRUNCATE` + `DescriptorFlags::READ` returns `Err(ErrorCode::NotPermitted)`, then re-checks contents.

Both bins build cleanly for `wasm32-wasip1`, and `wasmtime-wasi` type-checks. The `PREVIEW1_FILE_TRUNCATION_READONLY*` / `PREVIEW2_FILE_TRUNCATION_READONLY_COMPONENT` constants are auto-generated by the artifacts build script from these bin filenames.

### Not modified (per the CRITICAL instruction)
I left everything under `tests/` alone — the placeholder `wasi-common` tests and the `wasi` test runners live in `tests/` directories and will be supplied by the verification system's test patches.
